title: A Splash server bound to 0.0.0.0 is invisible to the launcher (Host 403)
description:
Splash validates the HTTP Host header and never accepts a wildcard: server/server.py FrontendServer builds allowed_hosts from --allowed-host, the bind address, localhost, 127.0.0.1 and ::1, and drops 0.0.0.0 and :: (so --allowed-host 0.0.0.0 cannot fix it). The launcher probes an instance at its configured host:port, so with the stock host: "0.0.0.0" every Splash probe sends Host: 0.0.0.0:<port> and gets 403 Forbidden (Server: Splash).

Observed 2026-09-24 on the live config (defaults host 0.0.0.0, port 1111, profile Qwen3.8-27B-Splash, repo build at 3e07fd6+): curl http://127.0.0.1:1111/ready -> 200, http://0.0.0.0:1111/ready -> 403. Consequences:
- status / the TUI report "No servers running" while Splash is Ready.
- load fails with "server at 0.0.0.0:1111 did not become healthy within 30s" although it is up.
- stop splash cannot identify it; the server had to be stopped with kill -TERM <pid>.
- auto_stop_server cannot sweep it, so a llama.cpp load onto the shared port hits the port-conflict refusal.

Affected: Splash.HealthCheck, Splash.StartingUp and Splash.ListRunningModels (openAIModelList) in internal/launcher/backend_splash.go, called with the configured addr by discovery, the start-path health wait and identifyBackend. llama-server, Ollama and LM Studio don't check Host, so only Splash is affected.

Suggested fix: Splash's HTTP probes dial the loopback address when the configured host is a wildcard (0.0.0.0 -> 127.0.0.1, :: -> [::1]), keeping the instance keyed by its configured address (ADR-0006). Test: httptest server that 403s unless Host is loopback, probed as 0.0.0.0:<port>. The integration test missed this because it binds 127.0.0.1; add a 0.0.0.0 case.

Separate but related: a LAN hostname (e.g. Apollo-II.local) also gets 403 unless passed via extra_args --allowed-host. The live profile now does this; README / example-config Splash notes should mention it.

Related: llama-launcher-splash-loading-invisible (loading window; a different cause).

title: CHANGELOG: add the log-redaction Security entry
description:
The log-redaction change has no changelog entry because `CHANGELOG.md` has no `## [Unreleased]` heading (`CHANGELOG.md:3`); the release step must add it under Security:

- **Log output masks API keys** — `llama-launcher logs`, the menu's *Show log*, the start-crash log tail, and the MCP `tail_log` tool now replace the backend's configured key and any `--api-key` value with `[redacted]`. Unconditional defense in depth: no tested llama-server build echoes its keys, but a future build or wrapper script that does can no longer leak them through a log view. Log files on disk are unchanged.

title: CHANGELOG: correct the 1.7.0 llamacpp extra_args --api-key claim
description:
`CHANGELOG.md:17` (released 1.7.0 Security entry) still says llama-server reads `LLAMA_API_KEY` only when no `--api-key` flag is present, "so a user's own `extra_args` override still wins". `TestLlamaServerAPIKey` showed the opposite on b10851: the flag's key is appended, both keys authenticate. The corrective entry could not be applied because `CHANGELOG.md` has no `## [Unreleased]` heading (`CHANGELOG.md:3`); the release step must add it under the new version heading:

- **Corrected: an `extra_args` `--api-key` for llamacpp does not replace the configured `api_key` — both keys are accepted.** The 1.7.0 notes said an override would win; the new integration test (`TestLlamaServerAPIKey`, `make test-integration`) found the flag's key appended to the environment key on llama.cpp b10851, so both authenticate. To change the key, change `api_key` rather than adding an override. The same test found neither key echoed into llama-server's own log file. README and TDD now say so.

Origin: deferred from the api-key residue and doc-fixes plan.

title: Confirm llama.cpp --api-key append-vs-replace semantics
description:
llama.cpp appends `--api-key` values rather than replacing, so an `extra_args` override likely makes both keys valid rather than the override strictly winning; confirm against `common/arg.cpp` before the release. The comment asserting that the override wins is at `internal/launcher/backend_llamacpp.go:153`.

Origin: deferred from the security-hardening and key-migration plan.
notes:
2026-09-24: settled empirically on llama-server b10851 (commit 67672dc5b) by `TestLlamaServerAPIKey` (`internal/launcher/server_integration_test.go`, `make test-integration`): llama.cpp **appends** — with `LLAMA_API_KEY` from the launcher and `--api-key` from `extra_args`, **both keys are valid** (each answers 200 on `/v1/models`, a wrong key 401). An override therefore never revokes the configured key; this is the fact the unconditional log redaction guards against. The same run found neither key echoed into llama-server's own log file. The `backend_llamacpp.go` comment, README, and TDD §4.2 are corrected; the released 1.7.0 CHANGELOG entry still carries the old claim.

2026-09-24: api-key-residue-doc-fixes plan (bee1a08) landed the confirmation and the code/README/TDD corrections; left open until the corrective CHANGELOG entry for `CHANGELOG.md:17` is applied.

title: A loading Splash server is invisible to Starting detection and stop
description:
Splash binds its port only after the model loads (manual probe during the splash-backend plan's item 6: connection refused on /ready, then /ready 200, never a 503), so the plan's "/ready 503 while loading" fact does not hold. A loading Splash is invisible to address-keyed Starting detection and Stop (ADR-0010): Splash.StartingUp (internal/launcher/backend_splash.go:65) never answers true, so discovery's Starting fallback (internal/launcher/discovery.go:138), the start path's still-starting refusal (internal/launcher/server.go:78) and the stop path's Starting check (internal/launcher/server.go:254) do not see it.

Origin: deferred from docs/plans/archived/2026-09-24 - 00 - splash-backend-plan.md (item 6).

title: api_key_cmd re-runs on every menu probe tick
description:
`Config.Reload()` runs on every menu probe tick, so with `api_key_cmd` set an entry's command re-runs every refresh interval while the menu is open — contradicting the "one subprocess per configured entry per run" wording; caching or a per-open resolve may be wanted (`internal/launcher/menu.go:874`).

title: An IPv6 host builds an unparseable address (host:port without brackets)
description: Every address is built as fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", host, port) — internal/launcher/discovery.go (RunningInstance.Addr, probeInstance), config.go, server.go (start path, still-starting refusal, LoadProfile target), cli.go. An IPv6 host such as "::" or "::1" yields ":::8000" / "::1:8000", which net.SplitHostPort rejects and an http URL cannot carry, so every probe, lsof lookup and stop against an IPv6-configured instance misbehaves. Fix: net.JoinHostPort at every producer. Found by the regression check of docs/plans/2026-09-24 - 01 - splash-wildcard-host-probe-plan.md, which scopes its wildcard fix to 0.0.0.0 and an empty host because of this.

title: TestStopServerAt_StartingOccupant hard-fails without lsof
description:
`TestStopServerAt_StartingOccupant` depends on a working `nc` listener and fails in containers without it — pre-existing and environment-dependent. It skips when `nc` is missing but hard-fails when `findListeningPID` never matches, which is what a container without `lsof` produces (`internal/launcher/server_test.go:1580`).

title: Propagate ErrUnsupported on the two Windows paths
description:
`ErrUnsupported` does not survive two Windows paths (TDD §16.6): `connectExternalServer` replaces Ollama's `TryStart` refusal with its own "not reachable … start it manually" message, and the stop verbs never reach a seam function (`IsProcessAlive` is false there), ending at "PID could not be determined". Propagating the sentinel would be additive and would not change macOS behaviour — but there is no Windows host to prove it against.
